title: The Palimpsest of Memory
text:
Memoir, at its best, is less an archive of events than an act of excavation. The writer who sets out to recall a childhood summer discovers that memory is a palimpsest, each recollection written over earlier and fainter versions of itself. My grandmother's kitchen, for instance, exists in my mind as a composite of several decades rather than any single afternoon. Yet I have come to believe that these distortions are precisely what make the story honest.

The prose itself must therefore carry a certain reticence, a refusal to pretend that the past can be restored intact. Writers who approach their material with meticulous care often produce work that feels more truthful than strictly chronological accounts. Nostalgia, when handled well, becomes a lens rather than a sentimental blur. The result is a text that admits its own incompleteness, and in admitting it, earns the reader's trust.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, how is memory described?
options: As a palimpsest, with earlier recollections written over
As a perfectly preserved archive of events
As a reliable record of a single afternoon
As a diary written in a single moment

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what kind of work often feels more truthful?
options: Work by writers who approach material with meticulous care
Texts that pretend the past can be restored intact
Accounts that rely on sentimental blur

questions.text: What does the author suggest about memoirs that admit their own distortions?
options: They are less trustworthy than traditional histories
They earn the reader's trust through honesty about their limits
They avoid any discussion of the past
They rely mainly on exact chronology

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of nostalgia?
options: It should be removed from writing entirely
It is useful only when it is examined carefully rather than indulged
It always distorts the truth beyond repair
It is valuable mainly for readers, not for writers

a tendency not to reveal feelings or information
very careful and precise about details
the act of digging out and examining something that is buried

paragraph_translations: Мемуари в найкращому випадку є не стільки архівом подій, скільки актом розкопок. Письменник, який береться відтворити літо свого дитинства, виявляє, що пам'ять — це палімпсест, де кожен спогад записано поверх давніших, блідіших версій самого себе. Кухня моєї бабусі, наприклад, існує в моїй уяві як поєднання кількох десятиліть, а не як один окремий вечір. Проте я дійшов висновку, що саме ці спотворення роблять історію чесною.

Тому сама проза мусить зберігати певну стриманість, відмову вдавати, що минуле можна відновити цілком. Письменники, які ставляться до свого матеріалу з ретельною увагою, часто створюють твори, що видаються правдивішими за суворо хронологічні розповіді. Ностальгія, коли з нею працюють добре, стає лінзою, а не сентиментальним розмиттям. Результат — текст, який визнає власну неповноту, і, визнаючи її, здобуває довіру читача.
